name: Project-End Report
one_liner: The project's own post-mortem: what worked, what didn't, and what the organisation should do next.
purpose: Following the Project-End Review Meeting, the overall experience of the project is summarised in a report that documents best practices, Lessons Learned, pitfalls and solutions to problems. The report should be used as a knowledge base for future projects. The template adds that its goal is to capture overall stakeholder satisfaction, evaluate the project experience, and offer post-project recommendations.
created_in: Closing Phase — written after the Project-End Review Meeting
approved_by: Project Steering Committee (PSC) is Accountable; the Project Owner (PO) gives final project approval at Administrative Closure

Quality Assurance and Quality Control outputs
feeds: Post-Project Recommendations to the permanent organisation

traps: PSC is Accountable here, not the PO — the PO is only Consulted. The PO's moment is Administrative Closure.
Written after the Project-End Review Meeting, not instead of it; the meeting's MoM is the main input.
Guide p.66 and summary table p.112 both print I A C S C C R C — no dashes.
Lessons Learned should be collected as they arise; leaving them to Closing loses them in long projects.
Benefits often cannot be measured at closure — handing benefit tracking to the permanent organisation is correct, not a failure.

castor_excerpt.title: Extract — Project-End Report, Project CASTOR, issued 19 Jul 2028 after the Project-End Review Meeting of 12 Jul 2028
rows: Four of five success criteria met at go-live: SC1 disbursement cycle time cut from 5 working days to 1; SC2 post-disbursement reconciliation same-day; SC4 manual re-keying down from ~1.400 fields per quarter to 0; SC5 both open internal-audit findings on LOS closed. SC3 (new instrument onboarding in 6 weeks) is demonstrated but not yet proven in production.

Cost: final €8,96 m against a baselined €8,4 m, +6,7%. Effort: 3.307 PD against 3.100 PD. Schedule: go-live achieved on the baselined date of 15 May 2028 after the +1 month forecast slip reported on 31 Mar 2027 was recovered. Scope: 11 approved changes, 2 postponed, 1 rejected; none altered the Business Case.

R-07 — loss of Levallois's key architect — was identified during Planning and materialised on 04 Oct 2027. It moved from the Risk Log to the Issue Log as I-12. The retention and knowledge-transfer clause negotiated at contract award on 18 Sep 2026 limited the loss to four weeks. R-03, non-ratification of the ESM Treaty reform, never materialised and was accepted throughout.

The Board of Directors cabinets were not on the Project Stakeholder Matrix. The verbal request of 09 Mar 2027 that became CR-007 was the consequence. Lesson: map the cabinets as stakeholders from Initiating.

The largest conflict was ownership of the retraining of 40 loan administrators — Transition Plan or Business Implementation Plan. It was settled in the Business Implementation Plan under the BM, and never needed change control.

Marie Curie (UR) refused acceptance of the reconciliation report on 27 Apr 2028 when the parallel run overlapped an EFSF bond rollover. Partial acceptance was granted and full acceptance followed on 05 May 2028. The Deliverables Acceptance Plan handled this correctly.
Parallel run with LOS ran 08 Jan – 30 Apr 2028 with no disbursement failures. Transition to operations on 15 May 2028; LOS decommissioned 30 Jun 2028.

40 loan administrators retrained by 30 Apr 2028 under the Business Implementation Group led by Grace Hopper. Two roles were redesigned; segregation of duties is now enforced by the platform rather than by procedure.
Levallois Systems delivered both releases on their baselined dates. Estimating on data migration was optimistic: WP4 closed at 85% budget performance.

Governance: a verbal scope request must become a Change Request Form before any estimating effort is spent — this saved 145 PD on CR-007. Project management: the monthly one-page Status Report kept the PSC out of task-level detail. Risk: contractual retention clauses are a usable risk response for key-person risk.

Benefits SC1–SC5 can only be measured over a full 2029 reporting year. Benefit tracking is handed to the Lending Operations Division under the PO. Follow-up project proposed: onboard the common backstop instrument within 6 weeks of the ESM Treaty reform entering into force, reusing the configuration engine and re-opening CR-007.
